questions.question: A client SYN uses sequence 1000. What is its next sequence position after establishment, before application data?
questions.explanation: SYN consumes one position in the client sequence space.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: A server SYN ACK uses sequence 7000 and acknowledgment 1001. What does the client acknowledge in the last handshake segment?
questions.explanation: The server SYN consumes one server sequence number.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: A segment starts at sequence 1001 and carries 26 payload bytes. What cumulative ACK covers all those bytes?
questions.explanation: Bytes 1001 through 1026 are covered; 1027 is next expected.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: What does a TCP cumulative acknowledgment number identify?
options: A) The number of complete SMTP messages
B) The next byte expected in that stream direction
C) The number of Ethernet switches visited
D) The segment ordinal number
questions.explanation: TCP acknowledgments refer to stream byte positions, not application message counts.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: Segment 2 is missing but segment 3 has arrived. Why can the application still be blocked?
options: A) IP prohibits receiving any out-of-order packet
B) The receiver must discard every later segment immediately
C) TCP cannot deliver an uninterrupted stream past the missing byte range
D) SMTP must issue another DNS request for segment 3
questions.explanation: TCP can buffer out-of-order bytes while withholding data beyond the stream gap.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: Which mechanism protects a slow receiver from being overwhelmed?
options: A) The advertised receive window rwnd
B) The IP TTL
C) The DNS TTL
D) The Ethernet source field
questions.explanation: Flow control limits sending based on the receiving endpoint buffer state.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: What is the distinct purpose of the congestion window cwnd?
options: A) To identify the receiving mailbox
B) To describe only free application buffer space
C) To constrain load offered to the network
D) To encrypt TCP options
questions.explanation: Congestion control responds to network load; receiver flow control has a different purpose.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: If rwnd is 32 KiB, cwnd is 12 KiB, and 8 KiB are in flight, how much new data fits under the simplified window bound?
options: A) 12 KiB
B) 24 KiB
C) 32 KiB
D) 4 KiB
questions.explanation: The outstanding limit is min(32,12)=12 KiB, leaving 4 KiB beyond the 8 KiB already outstanding.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: What is the minimum ordinary TCP header length?
options: A) 20 bytes
B) 8 bytes
C) 14 bytes
D) 40 bytes
questions.explanation: The base TCP header is 20 bytes; options increase it.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: What does TCP data offset 5 mean?
options: A) The TCP header occupies five 32-bit words, or 20 bytes
B) The payload starts at stream byte five
C) The IP packet traversed five routers
D) Five SMTP commands are included
questions.explanation: Data offset is a header-length field measured in 32-bit words.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: Which fields contribute to the TCP checksum pseudoheader?
options: A) Ethernet source, destination, and FCS only
B) Only IP TTL and header checksum
C) Only the SMTP Subject and Date fields
D) IP source, IP destination, protocol, and TCP length
questions.explanation: The pseudoheader binds checksum computation to relevant network-layer addressing and length information.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: What property does a TCP checksum supply?
options: A) Encryption of all message content
B) Detection of accidental corruption, rather than cryptographic authentication
C) Proof that a specific human sent a message
D) Guaranteed recovery without retransmission
questions.explanation: The checksum is an error-detection mechanism and is not a cryptographic integrity or identity guarantee.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: What is the relationship between QUIT and FIN?
options: A) QUIT and FIN are two spellings of the same TCP flag
B) FIN proves SMTP accepted the message
C) QUIT is an SMTP command, while FIN closes one TCP sending direction
D) QUIT changes the IP Protocol field from TCP to UDP
questions.explanation: Application dialogue and transport closure operate at different boundaries.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: Why is closing commonly described as separate in each direction?
options: A) TCP is full duplex and either endpoint can finish sending independently
B) TCP carries only one direction at a time
C) Every FIN opens an additional email connection
D) Ethernet requires two different SMTP servers
questions.explanation: Each stream direction can end separately and FIN consumes a sequence number.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: Does receipt of a single out-of-order later segment necessarily trigger classic fast retransmit?
options: A) Yes; every out-of-order segment triggers it immediately
B) Yes; the receiving application retransmits the missing packet
C) No; TCP never retransmits until a new connection is created
D) No; the classic duplicate-ACK trigger commonly requires three duplicate ACKs
questions.explanation: One later segment may produce only one duplicate ACK; timers or other implemented recovery can matter.

source.section: Section 7 — TCP connection reliability and control

questions.question: Which conclusion about TCP PSH is correct?
options: A) It terminates the SMTP DATA transaction
B) It forces one complete command per application read
C) It changes the destination port to the receiving mailbox
D) It does not define an SMTP message boundary
questions.explanation: Applications must use their own framing regardless of PSH.
